facts.content: Patient reports 2-day history of lower abdominal suprapubic pain just below the umbilicus.
facts.source_text: CC: 2-day lower abdo pain (suprapubic, just below umbilicus)

facts.content: The abdominal pain is constant and burning, worse and tender to pressure.
facts.source_text: constant, burning; worse; tender to pressure

facts.content: Patient reports feeling hot and sweaty without a measured temperature.
Patient has mild nausea.
Patient has increased urinary frequency.
Patient reports pink urine suggesting possible hematuria.
Patient denies pain on urination.
Patient has not vomited.
Patient reports that bowel movements are now normal after constipation last week.
facts.source_text: bowels now normal after constipation last week

facts.content: Patient reports no diarrhea.
Patient denies shortness of breath and cough.
Patient denies palpitations.
Patient denies headache and vision changes.
Patient reports being generally well.
Patient has had no prior similar episodes of the current problem.
Patient has an Implanon (etonogestrel) contraceptive implant in place.
Family history is negative for known bowel or gynecologic issues.
Patient lives with two roommates.
Patient works as an accountant.
Patient is a non-smoker.
Patient drinks alcohol socially.
Patient denies shortness of breath and cough in the review of systems.
Patient denies palpitations in the review of systems.
Patient denies headache and vision changes in the review of systems.
Patient is sexually active with the same partner.
Last sexual intercourse was 4 days ago.
Sexually transmitted infection screen about 6 months ago was normal.
Patient uses Implanon for contraception, inserted about one year ago.
Patient is still menstruating.
Last menstrual period was about two weeks ago.
Pregnancy is considered unlikely but possible.
Clinician assesses suprapubic abdominal pain for two days with urinary frequency, pink urine, mild nausea, subjective fevers, and no dysuria or vomiting.
facts.source_text: 1) Suprapubic abdo pain x2 days with urinary frequency and pink urine; mild nausea; subjective fevers; no dysuria/vomiting.

facts.content: Clinician impression is likely uncomplicated cystitis or urinary tract infection with possible hematuria.
facts.source_text: Likely uncomplicated cystitis/UTI with possible hematuria.

facts.content: Pregnancy status is considered uncertain due to recent last menstrual period, contraceptive implant, and sexual activity four days ago.
facts.source_text: 2) Pregnancy status uncertain (LMP ~2 wks ago; on implant; SA 4 days ago).

facts.content: Start trimethoprim one tablet twice daily for three days for urinary tract infection, with electronic prescription sent to the pharmacy.
facts.source_text: UTI: Start trimethoprim 1 tab BID x3 days; eRx to pharmacy

facts.content: Recommend paracetamol as needed for symptom relief.
Advise the patient to hydrate.
Cranberry juice may be taken if desired for symptomatic relief.
A urine pregnancy test is recommended to confirm that the patient is not pregnant.
facts.source_text: Testing: Urine pregnancy test recommended to confirm not pregnant

facts.content: Patient is advised to return or go to the emergency department if pain worsens, fever persists, vomiting develops, or there is no improvement.
facts.source_text: Safety net: Return/ED if worsening pain, persistent fever, vomiting, or no improvement

facts.content: If not improving, patient should follow up in a few days.
facts.source_text: otherwise f/u in a few days if not improving
